tool_args.rationale: The open-branch probe produced substantially higher output at low sink gradient than at high gradient, while the fixed-gradient input response rises and saturates. This is consistent with the bridge-mapped two-layer siphon plus a positive square-root branch. Fit its three parameters numerically to all seven rows; no further measurement is warranted.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Observed s_grad already spans 0.2 to 2.3, and there is no evidence of the specified avalanche threshold above 2.36.
All observed rows use the same H and initial memory/state; the signatures and input-response shape favor the static bridge-siphon family, not a trajectory-identification problem.

Possible nonlinear competitor, but bridge-supply signature plus clear s_grad suppression and an open-branch response support the simpler node-C bridge mapping; one more probe is not justified by current evidence.
No horizon variation or slow-horizon reversal evidence; pilot horizon is within the short range.
